title: Terraform module for GPU fleet with hybrid autoscaling and safe upgrade hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready Terraform module that provisions and manages a GPU fleet inside Private (VPC) deployments with a hybrid autoscaling strategy (ASG-backed steady capacity + Karpenter for burst/fast-scaling). The module should encapsulate lifecycle, health checks, IAM, and rolling upgrade hooks so Private customers can subscribe to a predictable, secure GPU pool that supports safe upgrades and automated remediation.

Scope and features:
- Create a reusable Terraform module that can create either: (a) ASG-based managed node groups for reserved capacity, (b) Karpenter Provisioner configuration for burst/spot capacity, or (c) both together with routing policies.
- Support mixed-instance families (e.g., nvidia-a100, g5, g4dn) via an instance_type_map input.
- Expose inputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, cluster_name, taints/labels for GPU nodes, instance_type_map, min/max/desired for ASG, karpenter_provisioner_enabled, spot_fallback_policy, node_volume_size_gb, gpu_profile (driver + toolkit), asg_lifecycle_hooks_config, upgrade_stagger_minutes, pre_drain_script_url.
- Implement health checks: EC2 instance status, kubelet Ready gating, and a lightweight node-exporter metric threshold (GPU memory pressure). Health check failures should create alerts and trigger ASG replacement or Karpenter remediation hooks depending on node ownership.
- Rolling upgrade strategy: Terraform-driven AMI/launch-template updates should invoke a staged rolling update flow: cordon -> pre-drain hook (call pre_drain_script to flush local caches, notify services) -> drain with graceful timeout -> terminate -> wait for new node Ready -> post-upgrade validation (kubelet + GPU probe). Provide a toggle to run the flow as an automated pipeline step vs manual runbook.
- Lifecycle hooks: integrate ASG lifecycle hooks for graceful termination with SQS + lambda hook to run pre-drain actions where needed. For Karpenter, provide an annotation-based pre-drain webhook config.
- Observability: emit tags and outputs required by Redwood Console: node_group_id, asg_ids, karpenter_provisioner_name, iam_instance_profile, security_group_ids. Provide Terraform outputs and instructions to attach CloudWatch dashboards and Prometheus scrape relabel rules.
- Security / IAM: least-privilege IAM roles for instance profile, SSM access for remote troubleshooting, and KMS policy for node bootstrap secrets. Mark module as security_review_required.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module deploys successfully in a test Private VPC with reserved + burst capacity.
- Autoscaling test: simulate load and verify Karpenter provisioner creates burst nodes under 120s and ASG scales as configured.
- Upgrade test: run the rolling upgrade, confirm pre-drain hook runs, no pods are forcefully killed, and metrics show <1% request error increase.
- Health check remediation: simulate kubelet failure, verify node is replaced and alert is sent to PagerDuty.
- Module publishes outputs and example usage in examples/ with terraform workspace instructions.

Implementation notes & constraints:
- The module must be agnostic to cloud provider where practical, but implementation will target AWS first (ASG, Launch Templates, SQS lifecycle hooks, EC2 health checks). Abstract provider-specific bits behind variable flags to allow later Azure/GCP ports.
- Keep module composable: do not bake cluster creation. Accept existing EKS/cluster identifiers.
- Avoid large provider/provider-specific remote-exec scripts inside module; prefer bootstrap from a signed S3 object (pre_drain_script_url) and SSM RunCommand for on-demand ops.
- Coordinate with infra quota team for instance limits during QA.
